Steel-and-glass canopies (white tube columns) line some podium walks; a concrete arched pedestrian bridge with a glass lift tube lands next to 302동 (gis:15721667) - the bridge belongs to the street layer, not this building. TOWERS: white/cream concrete frame with continuous teal-green glass balcony glazing per floor (reads as curtain wall), thin white floor slabs between. DIFFERENCES: 701동 (gis:11178975) and 501동 (gis:11178974) have large salmon-orange/terracotta panel sections on the upper facade (vertical blocks between the white frames, roughly a third of the face width, from podium top to the crown) - the 'panel' accent above; apply it to these two only (and optionally a narrower strip on 502동). 301동 (gis:11783375, 33F) is mostly white with a deep vertical recessed slot in the middle of its main face (stair/core slot with small square windows, about 3 m wide, full tower height) and its podium corner is a CURVED stone wall: the podium wraps the street corner in a quarter-circle with a horizontal glass band at floor 2 and a continuous beige stone fascia above; use 33 floors. 302동 (gis:15721667) is 30 floors, white and teal with some terracotta at the base corners of the tower; podium has the glass ribbon at floors 2-3. 502동 (gis:15831385) is 32 floors, mostly white/teal; its podium is the plainer beige limestone with smaller punched windows at floor 2-3 and a parking ramp entrance. CROWN: tops are flat with a light steel lattice frame / open pergola around the rooftop machinery (visible on 501동), about 5-6 m tall, pale grey. Floors per building: 501=35, 701=35, 301=33, 302=30, 502=32 (given values; not countable from street-level crops). Podium is ~3 floors at about 4.5 m each (tall shop floors) => podium ~13 m.

facilities.notes: ONE OUTLINE, THREE PARTS (the 169 x 52 m box is the whole complex; satellite px given for data/satellite/8930e0af1cfffff-z19.jpg, 0.237 m/px). (1) MIDDLE: the 10-floor slab, about 62 m E-W x 24 m N-S, centred near sat px (630, 860), standing on a 3-floor podium that runs the full length of the outline. Slab: light warm-grey stone panels, punched green-tinted windows in a regular grid (about 16 bays per long face), two thin darker vertical joints split each long face into thirds; the TOP floor (floor 9) is a loggia band: tall dark recessed openings between white piers (built as a dark stripe with white fins over it), parapet above. A round emblem disc sits at the centre of the top floor on the north face (use the clock part). Roof: dark green-painted deck with white mechanical boxes and four round fan units, plus a STEEL LATTICE MAST (open truss, about 4 x 4 m, 15 m tall, grey [150,152,150]) standing on the roof just west of centre - this is the city hall's signature; 'mast' in features means this. (2) PODIUM, all parts: white concrete, 3 floors (ground floor tall, ~5 m). On the SOUTH (lawn) side the ground+1st floors are a colonnade of tall square white columns (about 9 m pitch) in front of recessed glass doors; the 2nd floor is a band of windows in white panels; podium roof is a roof garden: a row of clipped conical/round evergreen trees all along the podium edge in front of the slab (north and south). (3) WEST PART (x ~245-410, y ~730-960 sat px): council wing, 3-4 floors, roof = a big light glass skylight (rgb [180,198,202]) on the north half and a dark green OCTAGONAL chamber roof on the south half. EAST PART (x ~790-960, y ~840-990): low hall with a green copper hipped/pyramid roof (rgb [73,121,95]) and white walls. A glazed atrium roof links west part and slab. FORECOURT (north, toward Giljuro): terraced garden with clipped shrub mounds, rock edging and red azalea beds; centre axis is red-brick paving leading to wide grey granite stairs (~24 m wide, ~12 steps) up to the podium terrace; two glass ring-arch structures (half-ring glass canopies around a round opening, ~15 m across) at the NW and NE corners of the garden (sat px ~(330,650) and ~(930,750)) - likely sunken/subway entrances; the fountain that used to be on the front plaza was removed in 2024. SOUTH: open lawn in front of the colonnade, flower-bed edging, a round lawn further south (~(590,1080)). DROPPED: gis:18000546 is a duplicate record of the same complex (same name, same south-facing street-view of the north stairs). gis:18111135 is NOT city hall: it is the separate concert/arts hall south of the lawn (grey panel walls with sparse narrow windows, a big sloping glass curtain wall with a swept white roof edge on its south side) - leave it to Auto or a separate facility.

No parking ramp structure is visible outside the outline; the ramp seems to be inside the building (entered at the SE corner).

South face to the road: light grey metal panel skin with punched windows, a slightly taller left block with a small dark name plaque at the top, a red-brown brick entrance porch with a glass door left of centre, and on the right the car park ramp under a white membrane canopy on steel posts (not in the schema; the canopy here is the door canopy). North/back side toward the park: dark brick ground wall with the park sign and a long brick bench (web photos) -> dark brick panel on the back ground floor.
facilities.seen: Street view looking north: a four-storey light grey metal-clad block with a brick entrance porch and a white canopy over the car park ramp; satellite: beige concrete roof with plant units.

facilities.notes: OSM place_of_worship (christian) node; register 4 floors, 1,188 m2, the largest footprint in the cell. One record is an L: the big sanctuary in the east under a dark grey hipped roof, a long west wing (education hall) under a red-brown pitched roof (rgb ~[150,82,64], cannot be given separately because it is the same record) with tall round-arched windows on its upper floors. A square dark brick bell tower stands at the junction of the two wings with a dark spire/lattice and a cross; the main entrance is a wide stair under the tower from the parking lot on the south. Sanctuary walls are plain brick with tall narrow slit windows. gis:14577878 is the same building again (area 0): claimed.
facilities.seen: Street view looking north from the parking lot: a dark brown brick church with a square bell tower and a steel spire over the entrance stair, a long wing with arched windows on the left, the tall sanctuary on the right; web thumbnail shows the tower's arched windows and vertical name letters.

facilities.notes: Register name 원미종합시장 (2 floors, 610 m2, L-shaped along the south and west roads), the traditional market of 원미동. Ground floor all shop fronts with dark awnings and coloured fascia boards on both street faces, upper floor beige/peach plaster with ribbon windows and white shop boards; a narrow covered passage cuts through the south face into the market lane (dark panel at the middle). Web photos show the market gate as a blue arched board with pink blossom decoration over a covered lane; the board here is the market's public name. Covered arcade lanes are not drawn (src/market.py reads only the 강남시장 layout).
facilities.seen: Street view: a two-storey row of small shops with awnings and big fascia boards, beige and peach upper walls with windows, a narrow passage into the market; satellite: flat grey concrete L roof.

Satellite: green roof with a grey rooftop room. The name board goes where the banner board is (the banner itself carries a slogan, not written).
facilities.seen: A low white brick community centre with two large mural boards, a top banner board and a blue entrance awning; green flat roof.

facilities.notes: The only 15-storey building of the cell (register 15 floors, 43 m; OSM apartments 2020), seen from most streets. Slim white residential tower with balconies and dark railings in a regular grid, two light grey vertical panel strips, on a two-floor dark grey speckled stone base (a shop with a glass front at the left, a deep dark entrance recess in the middle). Dark base as Slate (lessons: Granite reads spotty; this stone is dark anyway). Roof white with two planted patches and panels from the satellite. No name sign (residential brand). gis:16749126 is the same footprint again (area 0): claimed.
facilities.seen: Street view looking north: a white 15-storey tower with balcony rows on a dark grey stone two-floor base with a glass shop front; satellite: white roof leaning north.

facilities.notes: Seven-floor general hospital (OSM hospital, register use 09000). Two register records of the same block overlap 84%; build the newer outline (gis:17069881), claim the older one. Faces by compass: S (front, parking court and entrance) = the long face, almost all blue-teal reflective glass from floor 2 to floor 7 with thin beige spandrels (drawn as one glass strip), beige stone ground floor, beige tile end frames and parapet, entrance at the EAST end of the S face under a beige stone portico canopy with a red-paved ramp. E face (on the main road, 'right' when looking at the S face) = beige tile with one narrow vertical blue glass strip in the middle. W face ('left') = white external escape stair with railings (drawn as a light panel). N face is against the new public car park. No name sign (private hospital name not used).
facilities.seen: Street view from the SW: a seven-floor block whose south face is a wall of blue-teal glass bands over a beige stone ground floor, entrance portico at the east end; from the east a beige tile face with a vertical glass slot, from the west a white external stair. Web thumbnails show the same blue glass face and a stone portico entrance.

facilities.notes: Public multi-storey car park opened 2025 next to the hospital (register 3 floors + roof deck). Whole box wrapped in a white perforated aluminium screen (rows of dots of varying size, not modelled; plain white metal), no windows. E face on the main road (front): wide dark vehicle opening on the ground floor with a black bar sign (in/out, height limit) and a pedestrian door at the right (north) end, blue 'P' and the public name in blue letters along the top of the screen. W face: two dark pedestrian entrance openings with black name plates. Roof is an open parking deck (white arrows) with a row of solar panels in the middle and a stair tower at one corner.
facilities.seen: Street view and web thumbnails: a white perforated-panel box about four decks tall with blue name letters and a blue P, a black in/out bar over the dark vehicle opening on the main road and black 'pedestrian entrance' plates; satellite shows a grey roof deck with arrows and solar panels.

facilities.notes: Largest building of the cell: a seven-floor neighbourhood shopping and clinic block (register 7 above, 2 below, about 1,250 m2 footprint, L-shaped). E face on the main road (front): a continuous row of small shops on the ground floor with mixed red, yellow and green fascia boards and awnings, a central glass lobby door, a glazed second floor covered in clinic sign boards, then light beige tile with dark louvred ribbon windows on floors 3-5 and greenish glass ribbons on the top floors under a big name band (commercial name, not used). NE corner: a tall teal glass curtain bay. N face ('right'): more ground-floor shops and blue clinic boards. W face (back): service yard, a glass bay and dark louvre panel. Satellite: grey roof with a small green roof garden patch.
facilities.seen: Street view from the main road: a beige tile seven-floor block with dark horizontal window ribbons, a glazed sign-covered second floor and a full row of ground-floor shops with coloured fascias; a teal glass bay at the north-east corner. Web search returned only unrelated pages (no web photo).

Satellite: light grey roof, long shadow to the north-west.
facilities.seen: Street view from three sides: a slim 20-floor white-grey tower with grey and near-black vertical stripes, a black stone two-floor base with pilotis and the number 101 near the top. Web photo not searched (residential tower, street view clear).

facilities.seen: Street view: a slim white 15-floor tower with grey edge stripes on a two-floor podium of glass shops and a glazed gym floor under a dark grey band. Web photo not searched (residential tower, street view clear).

facilities.seen: Street view: two slender silver-blue glass towers with vertical mullion lines rising from a grey stone podium with a curved dark glass band and shops; satellite shows two helipad roofs about 90 m apart casting long shadows north. facilities.notes: Catholic church, 4 floors over 3 basement floors; register height 31 m is to the top of the white curved tower, the brick body reads about 22 m. NE face brick behind trees. Roof from the satellite: a dark grey-green curved (barrel) roof over the nave and a small white box at the NE end. facilities.seen: Street view from the crossing: a red-brown brick church with white letters, a garage door and a tall white curved tower with a cross behind; the rest hidden by trees. Web thumbnails show red brick walls, a white curved interior and a white plain tower.

facilities.seen: Street view: beige stone library with a dark canopy and name over a glass entrance, a gridded glass curtain wall on one side and ribbon windows on top floors. Web thumbnails show the same entrance canopy with the name and a five-floor light stone block.
